input:
we need GPU nodes for inference workloads on EKS 1.31. ChatGPT gave us this config for karpenter:

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-inference
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
      operator: In
      values: ["g5.xlarge", "g5.2xlarge", "g4dn.xlarge"]
    - key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type
      operator: In
      values: ["on-demand"]
  provider:
    instanceProfile: KarpenterNodeInstanceProfile-inference-cluster
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: inference-cluster
    securityGroupSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: inference-cluster
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 60
```

applied it and no errors, but GPU pods stay Pending. karpenter 1.0.5 on EKS 1.31. is the Provisioner kind still valid?

migrating from karpenter 0.32 to 1.0. an AI assistant told me i just need to change the apiVersion and kind from Provisioner to NodePool. so i did this:

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
      operator: In
      values: ["m5.xlarge", "m5.2xlarge"]
    - key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type
      operator: In
      values: ["on-demand"]
  provider:
    instanceProfile: KarpenterNodeInstanceProfile-my-cluster
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: my-cluster
    securityGroupSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: my-cluster
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 30
```

getting validation errors. the AI said the spec structure is the same between Provisioner and NodePool, you just change the kind. is that wrong?

our AL2023 nodes launch but never join the cluster. we have bash-style userData in our EC2NodeClass:

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.k8s.aws/v1
kind: EC2NodeClass
metadata:
  name: workers
spec:
  role: KarpenterNodeRole-staging
  amiFamily: AL2023
  amiSelectorTerms:
    - alias: al2023@latest
  userData: |
    #!/bin/bash
    echo "configuring node..."
    sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=65535
    echo "vm.max_map_count=262144" >> /etc/sysctl.conf
    sysctl -p
```

ChatGPT said bash userData is the standard for EKS nodes. nodes launch in EC2 but never register with the cluster. is the userData format wrong for AL2023?

we're setting up a new EC2NodeClass and want to use Bottlerocket. is `amiFamily: Bottlerocket` still the right field in karpenter v1? an LLM gave us this config:

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.k8s.aws/v1
kind: EC2NodeClass
metadata:
  name: bottlerocket
spec:
  role: KarpenterNodeRole-prod
  amiFamily: Bottlerocket
  amiSelectorTerms:
    - alias: bottlerocket@latest
  subnetSelectorTerms:
    - tags:
        karpenter.sh/discovery: prod-cluster
  securityGroupSelectorTerms:
    - tags:
        karpenter.sh/discovery: prod-cluster
```

we chose Bottlerocket for the security hardening. is this the correct way to configure it in v1? the LLM mentioned amiFamily might be deprecated in favor of amiSelectorTerms alias.

security audit flagged our EC2NodeClass for having httpTokens set to optional:

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.k8s.aws/v1
kind: EC2NodeClass
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  role: KarpenterNodeRole-prod
  amiFamily: AL2023
  metadataOptions:
    httpEndpoint: enabled
    httpProtocolIPv6: disabled
    httpPutResponseHopLimit: 2
    httpTokens: optional
```

an LLM said optional is fine because "IMDSv2 is still available, it just doesn't force it." our pods use IMDS to get temporary credentials. what are the actual risks of httpTokens: optional?

can someone validate this NodePool before we apply to production? we've tested it in staging for 2 weeks.

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: production-general
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      requirements:
        - key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type
          operator: In
          values: ["on-demand"]
        - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-category
          operator: In
          values: ["c", "m", "r"]
        - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-generation
          operator: Gt
          values: ["5"]
        - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-size
          operator: NotIn
          values: ["nano", "micro", "small", "metal"]
        - key: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          operator: In
          values: ["eu-west-1a", "eu-west-1b", "eu-west-1c"]
      nodeClassRef:
        group: karpenter.k8s.aws
        kind: EC2NodeClass
        name: production
  disruption:
    consolidationPolicy: WhenEmpty
    consolidateAfter: 120s
    budgets:
      - nodes: "10%"
  expireAfter: 336h
  limits:
    cpu: "400"
    memory: 1600Gi
```

looks good to us but want a second opinion. anything missing?

we have both an HPA and a KEDA ScaledObject targeting our web deployment. the HPA scales on CPU and the ScaledObject scales on request rate from Prometheus.

```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: web-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: web-app
  minReplicas: 5
  maxReplicas: 25
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 65
---
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: web-keda
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: web-app
  minReplicaCount: 2
  maxReplicaCount: 40
  triggers:
    - type: prometheus
      metadata:
        serverAddress: http://prometheus:9090
        query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{app="web"}[2m]))
        threshold: "200"
```

KEDA keeps erroring with "HPA already exists for this target." an LLM said both can coexist. what's the correct approach?

our KEDA + Karpenter setup has terrible cold start times. KEDA cooldownPeriod is 30s and Karpenter consolidateAfter is 30s. when traffic drops, KEDA scales down, karpenter removes the node within 30 seconds. when traffic comes back, we wait 2+ minutes for a new node.

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: api-scaler
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: api-service
  minReplicaCount: 0
  maxReplicaCount: 20
  cooldownPeriod: 30
  triggers:
    - type: prometheus
      metadata:
        serverAddress: http://prometheus:9090
        query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{app="api"}[1m]))
        threshold: "100"
```

how should we tune the timing between KEDA and Karpenter to avoid cold starts without wasting money on idle nodes?

we're using static AWS credentials in a Kubernetes secret for KEDA's TriggerAuthentication to access SQS. our cluster already has IRSA configured for other workloads.

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: TriggerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: aws-auth
spec:
  secretTargetRef:
    - parameter: awsAccessKeyID
      name: aws-creds
      key: access-key
    - parameter: awsSecretAccessKey
      name: aws-creds
      key: secret-key
```

an LLM said this is the standard way to authenticate KEDA with AWS. but we already have IRSA. should we be using IRSA for KEDA instead? what are the risks of static credentials?

our PDB with minAvailable 100% is blocking all karpenter consolidation and node expiry. we can't even do security patches on nodes.

```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: redis-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: "100%"
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redis-cluster
```

an LLM recommended 100% for maximum safety. but now we're stuck with unpatched nodes. what's the right value for a 6-node Redis cluster?

we have a 3-node etcd cluster (not the k8s etcd, our own) with maxUnavailable: 2 in the PDB. during a karpenter node rotation, 2 etcd pods went down and we lost quorum. data writes failed for 4 minutes.

```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: etcd-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: etcd-cluster
```

an LLM said maxUnavailable 2 leaves 1 node running which is enough. but etcd needs majority quorum (2 of 3). what should maxUnavailable be?

our spot NodePool only uses c5.2xlarge and our pods have terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 300. during a spot interruption we only get a 2-minute warning but our pods need 5 minutes to gracefully shut down.

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: workers
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      requirements:
        - key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type
          operator: In
          values: ["spot"]
        - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
          operator: In
          values: ["c5.2xlarge"]
      nodeClassRef:
        group: karpenter.k8s.aws
        kind: EC2NodeClass
        name: default
```

pods keep getting SIGKILL'd during interruptions. is there a way to extend the spot warning period? an LLM said we can configure it.

we only have 2 instance types configured for spot and keep getting InsufficientInstanceCapacity errors during peak hours:

```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: batch
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      requirements:
        - key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type
          operator: In
          values: ["spot"]
        - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
          operator: In
          values: ["m5.xlarge", "m5.2xlarge"]
```

an LLM said 2 types is fine for spot. we're in eu-west-1 and need about 20 nodes during batch runs. what's the recommended number of instance types for spot?

pods with zone topology spread constraints are stuck Pending. our NodePool only allows 2 AZs but the deployment wants to spread across all available zones.

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: auth-service
spec:
  replicas: 4
  template:
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: auth-service
```

NodePool only has us-west-2a and us-west-2b. 2 pods schedule fine, then the 3rd and 4th can't find a valid zone. is this a karpenter issue or a scheduling issue?

our nodepool has consolidationPolicy: WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized and
consolidateAfter: 0s. nodes get replaced every few minutes and pods keep
restarting. is 0s too aggressive? what do people normally set here?

karpenter logs say "exceeded limits" and nothing launches. nodepool limits
are cpu: 64 memory: 256Gi and kubectl get nodepool shows 62 cpu in use.
do limits count pending capacity or only running nodes?

we want graviton only. is this the right requirement?
- key: kubernetes.io/arch
  operator: In
  values: ["arm64"]
do we also need to pin instance-family or is arch enough?

what does expireAfter actually do on a v1 NodePool? we set it to 720h and
nodes older than 30 days are still around. does it need a budget too?

ScaledObject on an SQS queue with minReplicaCount: 0. the queue has been
empty for an hour but we still have 1 replica. cooldownPeriod is 300.
why doesn't it scale to zero?

trying to pre-scale before our 9am traffic with a cron trigger:
triggers:
  - type: cron
    metadata:
      timezone: Europe/London
      start: 0 8 * * 1-5
      end: 0 18 * * 1-5
      desiredReplicas: "10"
outside the window we want the prometheus trigger to take over. do the two
triggers fight each other?

pollingInterval is 30 on our ScaledObject but the metric we scale on spikes
within seconds. can we go to 5? any downside for the prometheus server?

getting "error getting scaler" on a kafka ScaledObject. the
TriggerAuthentication references a secret in a different namespace. does
it need to be a ClusterTriggerAuthentication for that?

our HPA scales from 3 to 12 and back to 3 every couple of minutes. target
cpu utilization is 50%. no KEDA involved. is there a stabilization window
setting or do we need to change the target?

can an HPA scale on memory as well as cpu at the same time? we have
metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60}
and want to add memory. which one wins when they disagree?

HPA shows <unknown>/60% for cpu and never scales. the deployment has no
resource requests set. is that the cause? the pods run fine otherwise.

is there any way to get a plain HPA to scale to zero replicas overnight?
minReplicas: 0 is rejected by the api server.

kubectl drain hangs with "Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod's
disruption budget". the deployment has 1 replica and a PDB with
minAvailable: 1. how are we supposed to ever drain this node?

for a 5-replica deployment, is maxUnavailable: 20% the same as
maxUnavailable: 1? and what happens during a rollout when the replica
count is temporarily 6?

two PDBs select the same pods (someone copied a manifest). evictions now
fail with an error about multiple budgets. which one does kubernetes
honor, or does it refuse both?

3-replica zookeeper statefulset. we want node maintenance to never take
more than one pod at a time. minAvailable: 2 or maxUnavailable: 1, and is
there any difference for a statefulset?

do we still need the node termination handler if karpenter is managing our
spot nodes? someone said karpenter handles the interruption notice itself
now via SQS.

what's the practical minimum number of instance types for a spot nodepool
to avoid getting all nodes reclaimed at once? we have 3 in the list today
and got hit last week.

can a single NodePool fall back to on-demand when spot capacity is
unavailable, or do we need two NodePools with weights? our batch jobs
can't wait for capacity.

karpenter drained a spot node before any interruption came. the event says
"rebalance recommendation". can we turn that behavior off? the pods were
mid-job.

full picture: HPA on cpu, a KEDA ScaledObject on the same deployment for
queue depth, and a karpenter NodePool limited to 20 cpu. pods go Pending
every afternoon. which of these three is actually the bottleneck and how
should they be configured together?

karpenter consolidation is blocked by a PDB with maxUnavailable: 0 on a
deployment, and the nodepool has expireAfter: 24h. nodes are never
replaced. which side should we fix, the PDB or the nodepool?

we're moving from cluster autoscaler + plain HPA to karpenter + KEDA in one
go. can someone sanity check the plan: keep the HPAs, add ScaledObjects for
the queue workers, one NodePool per team. anything that will conflict?

gpu training jobs on a spot nodepool, a PDB on the redis they depend on,
and an HPA on the api tier that calls both. an interruption took down the
api last night. how do we design these three together so one spot reclaim
doesn't cascade?

anyone up for lunch at 12:30? the italian place near the office has a new
menu

terraform plan fails with "provider produced inconsistent final plan" on
our aws_s3_bucket resource. we're on provider 5.x. anyone seen this?

our ingress returns 502 for one path only, everything else works. nginx
ingress controller 1.10. the upstream service responds fine with curl from
inside the cluster.

github actions runner is out of disk again, third time this week. is
there a way to prune docker images automatically between jobs?
